newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ merch trade balance trend still falling.
newsitem.headline: NZ merch trade balance trend still falling.

text.p: From a high point in October 1996, the trend in New Zealand's monthly merchandise trade balance continued to decline in May, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
From October last year to May, the imports trend averaged a monthly rise of 0.8 percent, while the exports trend averaged a monthly fall of 0.6 percent.
SNZ said unadjusted exports for May were worth NZ$2.09 billion, down 4.1 percent from May 1996. Unadjusted imports also fell over the same period, down 9.1 percent to $1.7 billion.
The trade surplus in May was NZ$406.5 million, against economists' average forecast of a $293.5 million surplus, and compared with a surplus of $327.1 million for May 1996.
The trade balance for the year ended May was in deficit to the value of NZ$460.6 million, versus economists' average expectation of a $563.3 million deficit.
SNZ said that excluding large irregular items such as aircraft and ships, the deficit for the May year would have been reduced to $355 million.

For the year ended May, unadjusted exports were worth $20.84 billion, up 0.7 percent on the previous May year. Exports of milk powder, butter and cheese showed the biggest growth over the period, up $618 million to $3.53 billion.
Significant falls were recorded for wood pulp, down 26.8 percent to $360 million, and wool, down 10.4 percent to $931 million.

Unadjusted imports for the year to May were worth $21.3 million, down 0.2 percent on the previous year. Mechanical machinery imports, valued at $3.32 billion, continued to lead import demand but were down 6.1 percent on the previous May year.
